title: OpenAI PR tells journalist to ‘move on’ while asking Sam Altman about a ChatGPT user’s suicide
key_facts: An OpenAI publicist tried to change the topic of OpenAI chief executive Sam Altman's interview with Vanity Fair's Mark Guiducci after the editor brought up a ChatGPT user's suicide.

Guiducci had asked Altman whether he knew Laura Reiley, a journalist who wrote an essay for The New York Times about her daughter's conversations with ChatGPT before the daughter took her own life; the publicist interrupted as he began to describe the case.

The publicist said they had two minutes left, that she wanted to be respectful but wanted to move on and talk about the future, and later that they really had to walk out the door in one or two minutes; Guiducci said he would finish his question first.
The interview continued, with Guiducci asking whether OpenAI planned to use ChatGPT conversations to shape its policies on a user's mental health crisis.

Altman said these are some of the hardest questions that anybody developing the technology faces and that releasing people's private data and hardest moments to researchers should probably not happen without their consent.
OpenAI spokesperson Drew Pusateri told The Verge the interview was running over, which is why the company asked to schedule even more time to continue after Altman addressed the topic.
The Verge article carries suicide and crisis helpline listings (US 988 lifeline, Crisis Text Line, Trevor Project and international lists).
